reactions.title: Iron wool burns in pure oxygen → Fe₂O₃
reactions.conditionLabel: Heated or ignited fine iron / steel wool in pure oxygen. This surface-form example does not imply that any bulk iron piece ignites immediately. The selected oxide is one reported endpoint; oxide mixtures may form. Conceptual model only.
observations: Heated iron wool burns brightly in oxygen with a shower of sparks.
The sparks are incandescent particles; the illustration represents burning iron, not a gas flame or an explosion.
A solid iron oxide remains; the selected equation is not a claim of a single exclusive oxide.
reactions.explanation: The fine strands expose a large surface to oxygen. Pure oxygen supports much more vigorous combustion than ordinary air. The bright glow and sparks represent heat and light released by oxidation. Oxide composition depends on the conditions.
